profiles.meeting_scenario: A regional bank's Strategy Analytics team is planning a six-week internal project to turn an academic market model on competing portfolios with polyvariant profit functions and 'zeitnot' client behavior into a decision memo for the retail investing business. The context is that the Head of Investments wants a practical recommendation on whether the bank should adjust promotional incentives for advisers before the next quarter's packaged-share campaign. The agenda is to agree on what the team will produce, how the model will be operationalized from the paper, who owns each workstream, and what timeline will be used for the executive readout. The expected outcome is a shared plan for a prototype analysis, a draft memo, supporting exhibits, and a final review cadence ahead of the quarter-planning deadline.

members.name: Priya Nair
members.expertise: Translating quantitative research into business recommendations, executive decision memos, and cross-functional planning
members.background: Priya spent seven years in banking strategy and previously worked in an internal consulting group supporting product and distribution teams; she is comfortable with statistical concepts but focuses on business framing, timelines, and executive usability.
members.private_state: Priya wants a credible, board-ready recommendation quickly and is trying to avoid an open-ended research effort; she is also concerned that senior leadership will reject anything that cannot be tied cleanly to current campaign planning and branch execution.
hidden_assumptions: A 'strategy analysis' deliverable naturally means an executive-facing recommendation package with a concise model appendix rather than a full technical reconstruction of the paper.
Using the 'current portfolio' means using the retail packaged-share book as it exists in this quarter's planning files, excluding closed legacy bundles and dormant accounts.

If they 'validate the model,' that means showing directional agreement on a recent holdout period and producing stable comparative scenarios, not proving the exact mathematical conditions from the paper.
A 'quarter-end readout' means materials must be effectively complete before the executive pre-read goes out on the Wednesday before the formal Friday planning meeting.

members.name: Daniel Cho
members.expertise: Stochastic processes, portfolio modeling, optimization, and implementation of research methods in banking analytics
members.background: Daniel has a PhD in applied probability and joined the bank from a capital markets modeling team; he is used to building technically faithful prototypes from published methods before simplifying them for business audiences.
members.private_state: Daniel wants to preserve methodological rigor and sees this as a chance to establish the analytics team's credibility with a more advanced optimization approach; he is worried that oversimplifying the paper will produce a recommendation that cannot be defended.
hidden_assumptions: A 'strategy analysis' plan should begin with a technically faithful implementation of the Markov-process method and only afterward be translated into executive language.
The 'current portfolio' refers to the full active-and-recently-active packaged-share dataset needed to estimate transition behavior, including legacy bundles if they affect switching patterns.

To 'validate the model' means checking whether the estimated process reproduces the paper's operating conditions and comparing solution behavior for monovariant and bivariant cases under the stated asymptotic assumptions.
A 'quarter-end readout' means the final presentation slot on Friday, so substantive modeling can continue through Thursday night as long as slides are assembled in time.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the strategy analysis
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to deliver a 'strategy analysis' for leadership.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this means a recommendation memo with a simplified model, a few scenarios on promotional incentives, and practical actions for the next campaign.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this means a technically faithful analysis of the published model, including reconstruction of the Markov method and comparison of monovariant versus bivariant profit-function cases before recommendations are distilled.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In business settings, 'strategy analysis' sounds broad enough to include both executive recommendations and technical work, so each hears their own normal meaning and sees no reason to clarify.

misalignment_points.topic: Which portfolio data is in scope
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to using the 'current portfolio' and 'recent campaign data.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the current quarter's retail packaged-share planning file used by the investments business, covering live products and adviser-managed campaign segments only.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the broader research dataset for the current portfolio environment, including active accounts plus recently retired package types and dormant-but-observed clients from the last 18 months.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both datasets are internally described as the current portfolio and recent campaign history, and because neither expects the other to mean a fundamentally different object, the label creates false alignment.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the prototype should be 'validated before the readout.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes validation is satisfied if the model gives sensible directional guidance on promotion versus missed-transaction fee tradeoffs and does not contradict observed business outcomes in a recent sample.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes validation requires demonstrating that the implementation behaves consistently with the theoretical conditions in the paper and that the optimization results are stable across monovariant and bivariant formulations under large-volume approximations.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Validation is a socially approved term that sounds rigorous to both sides, but each applies the standards common to their function, so the conversation proceeds without surfacing the different threshold.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both commit to having the readout ready by 'quarter-end Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes that quarter-end Friday refers to the executive planning meeting, which requires a polished pre-read and recommendation by the prior Wednesday afternoon.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes that quarter-end Friday is the actual delivery point, so analysis can be refined up to Thursday night and still count as on time.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have worked with recurring quarter-end routines but in different forums; the shorthand 'Friday' feels fully specified because each assumes the organizational calendar is shared.
